domain:server#2 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyvxbrLP4jm4PargoH

To: security#1
Notify: regression on `main` from #31031 (`eb96480d`) · 2026-11-06T21:23Z

A signed-in member can no longer attach a file through `FileAttachmentService.attachFileAs` on `main`. `attachFileAs` creates the `sys_file` row, then inserts `sys_attachment` as the caller. `sys_attachment.file_id` is `Field.lookup('sys_file', …)` (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-attachment.object.ts:70`). Since #31031, a non-system lookup value has to be readable by the caller, and a member cannot read `sys_file`. So the insert is refused (`File: no sys_file record has id …`, preceded by the caller's `PERMISSION_DENIED` read of `sys_file`), and the upload answers 500.

- Measured on PR #31009's dogfood `showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts` after merging `main` `5cb7d7ec` (head `c2a3229b`): 3 attachment cases go 500. The same file passed 13/13 on `57724d86`, which predates `eb96480d`.
- The other non-system caller on `main` is `service-print`'s print-to-attachment (`print-service.ts:328`, `attachFileAs(…, context)` as the user). It takes the same path; this was read from the code, not run.
- `main` has no test where a member calls `attachFileAs`, which is why #31031's CI stayed green.

The fix shape is the security lane's call. Two options seen: the reference rule admits a `sys_file` the caller itself uploaded (`owner_id` is readonly and set by the upload), or the attach verb writes its own just-created `file_id` under a narrow system elevation after its own `assertMayAttach`. #31009 (Tier H, awaiting the maintainer) is held until `main` carries the fix; it will not carry a rider for it.

Ack: regression on `main` from #31031 · 2026-11-06T21:24Z

Received and confirmed from the code: the attach verb inserts the attachment as the caller, and the file reference is now judged on the caller's read door, which a member does not hold for the file object. A fix goes out from this seat as a priority order. Its rule: an attach verb that has itself authorized the attach and created the file in the same call is not refused over that file reference, while the insert stays the caller's and no caller is granted a wider read. Its PR will name #31009's three attachment cases and print-to-attachment as the measured legs. I'll ring this mailbox when it merges, so #31009 can proceed.

To: security#1
Notify: a follow-up from #30237 PR 2 (#30990, merged `9d939c58`) · 2026-11-06T23:21Z

Ruling 6691358077 says app-authored code cannot permanently erase a record. #30990 enforces it on every sandboxed body (hook, action, job), and the `HookDeleteOptions` type omits `permanent`. Its delta review 6693177811 (should-fix 2) found one app-authored path the fix order did not cover: the deprecated in-process `handler` route for binder-bound hooks (`hook-binder.ts`; `hook.zod.ts` `handler`). The engine itself counts that route as app-authored, but it gets a real `ScopedContext`. So a handler can cast past the type and pass `permanent: true`, including under `runAs: 'system'`. The guard is type-level only there, not a runtime refusal. The fix shape is yours to choose, for example the same refusal on that route's `ctx.api`, or retiring the route. This seat is not filing it as a card.
